app.name: REDCAIRN
app.tagline: Tactical surface navigation for crewed Mars EVAs

site.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
site.locality: Floor of Jezero crater, beside Séítah
site.crs: IAU Mars 2000 geographic (EPSG:104905), planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude
rationale: Jezero is where Perseverance landed in February 2021, inside a crater that once held a lake, beside a river delta.
It has its own 1 m orbital elevation model and 25 cm photo (the maps Perseverance landed by), and a rover-driven track over the same ground.
Beta: built by the same scripts and engine as the Gale walk, to show the method works anywhere these four data sets exist.

elevationService.note: GET only; sends no CORS header, so sample at build time and ship the result as static data.

validation.method: Orbital DTM compared with nearby Perseverance waypoint elevations at EVA route locations; mean datum offset removed before calculating RMS

minerals.label: Mineral / science targets
minerals.status: live: waypoint and unit annotations from surface findings
minerals.note: Orbital spectrometer footprints (CRISM, about 18 m per pixel) are too coarse for a 1.5 km walk, so targets here are tied to what the rover measured on the ground.

units.label: Boxwork terrain
units.summary: Low ridges enclosing sandy hollows, in a layer rich in magnesium sulfates. Bedrock between the ridges carries white calcium sulfate veins.

units.label: Layered sulfate unit
units.summary: Layered sulfate-bearing bedrock above the boxwork terrain. The same unit was last sampled about 160 m lower on the mountain.

eva.name: Landing site to the first rock cores
eva.basis: Follows ground driven by Perseverance between mission sols 13 and 180, with spurs and back-tracks removed.

waypoints.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing

science.headline: The hatch
science.why: Perseverance landed here on 18 February 2021. The team named the spot for the science-fiction writer Octavia E. Butler.

pov.caption: The landing site, a few metres from where it touched down.

waypoints.story: Perseverance landed here on 18 February 2021. The team named the spot for the science-fiction writer Octavia E. Butler.

plain.title: The hatch
plain.see: Flat crater floor, scattered rock, the rim of Jezero on the horizon.
plain.why: Perseverance touched down here on 18 February 2021.
plain.teach: The colours classify slope only. Green is below 15°, amber is 15°–20°, and red exceeds 20°. Other hazards are not mapped.

waypoints.name: Van Zyl Overlook

science.headline: The overlook
science.why: On 19 April 2021 Perseverance parked here and watched Ingenuity, a 1.8 kg helicopter, rise three metres and hover. The first powered flight on another world.

pov.caption: Sol 58, the morning of the first flight. Its own tracks run off to the right.

waypoints.story: On 19 April 2021 Perseverance parked here and watched Ingenuity, a 1.8 kg helicopter, rise three metres and hover. The first powered flight on another world.

plain.title: The overlook
plain.see: The flat strip of ground where the first powered flight on another world took off.
plain.why: Perseverance watched Ingenuity fly from here.
plain.teach: The modeled ground here is below the 15° slope threshold. Loose soil, rocks and other hazards are not mapped.

waypoints.name: Máaz

science.headline: The crater floor
science.why: The team expected lake mud here. The floor turned out to be volcanic rock, later changed by water. The team named it Máaz, the Navajo word for Mars.

pov.caption: The crater floor on sol 117, looking north-east.

waypoints.story: The team expected lake mud here. The floor turned out to be volcanic rock, later changed by water. The team named it Máaz, the Navajo word for Mars.

plain.title: The crater floor
plain.see: Dark, flat rock and ripples of sand.
plain.why: The floor turned out to be volcanic rock, not lake mud.
plain.teach: The way home is already drawn from every point.

waypoints.name: Roubion

science.headline: Roubion
science.why: On sol 164 Perseverance drilled its first core here. The rock was too crumbly and fell away; the tube sealed with only Martian air inside. The team kept it anyway.

waypoints.story: On sol 164 Perseverance drilled its first core here. The rock was too crumbly and fell away; the tube sealed with only Martian air inside. The team kept it anyway.

plain.title: Roubion
plain.see: A pale paving stone of rock, drilled once.
plain.why: Its first sample attempt: the rock crumbled and the tube kept only air.
plain.teach: Purple: hills hide part of the sky, so less radiation.

waypoints.name: Rochette

science.headline: Rochette
science.why: On 1 and 8 September 2021 Perseverance drilled this ridge and sealed two cores, Montdenier and Montagnac: the first rock collected on another planet to be brought home.

waypoints.story: On 1 and 8 September 2021 Perseverance drilled this ridge and sealed two cores, Montdenier and Montagnac: the first rock collected on another planet to be brought home.

plain.title: Rochette
plain.see: A ridge of hard grey rock, two drill holes in its top.
plain.why: The first rock cores kept for return to Earth.
plain.teach: The way home is already on the map.

suit.note: Planning assumptions for the demo, not flight values. Each one is editable and labelled as simulated in the app.

speed.formula: kmh = suitFactor * baseKmh * exp(-k * abs(tan(slope) + offset))

suit.walkBackRule: Consumables remaining must always cover the walk back to the dock at current pace, plus the oxygen reserve.

radiation.backgroundBasis: Average galactic cosmic ray dose equivalent measured on the surface at Gale crater by the rover's radiation detector.
radiation.careerLimitNote: NASA career effective-dose limit for all astronauts, NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Revision B (2022).

terrainShielding.basis: Measured while the rover was parked at the foot of a cliff at Murray Buttes, 9–21 September 2016.
terrainShielding.model: Dose reduction = efficiency x fraction of sky hidden by terrain, scanned in 16 directions out to 80 m on the elevation grid.
terrainShielding.efficiencyNote: Assumption. Blocking sky does not remove ground-scattered particles, so only half the blocked fraction is credited.
candidates: Paniri butte (near WP5; to be located on the HiRISE mosaic)

scenarios.label: The real solar storm of September 2017
scenarios.basis: Replayed at its measured peak: during the solar particle event of 10-11 September 2017, Curiosity's RAD measured the surface dose rate at Gale rising two to three times above background over several hours (Zeitlin et al. 2018; Hassler et al. 2018). REDCAIRN uses the 3x peak for the whole drill, which is the cautious end.
scenarios.response: Recalculate the fastest modeled return under the scenario's terrain and consumable assumptions, and flag terrain shielding on the way.

scenarios.label: Dust storm
scenarios.basis: Rising atmospheric dust cuts visibility and solar power. Opacity values are demo assumptions.
scenarios.response: Reduce pace, tighten the walk-back margin and recommend return before visibility drops below waypoint spacing.

aiDisclosure: AI coding assistants were used to accelerate scaffolding, data retrieval scripts, code generation and review. All positions, elevations, imagery and mission findings come from the public sources listed. Suit telemetry and space-weather scenarios are simulated and labelled as such.

briefing.title: A rover walked this ground alone so that you would not have to.
body: For fourteen years one machine climbed this mountain at a few metres a day. Every place it stopped, it left a record: where it stood, how far it tilted, what the rock was made of, what the sky was doing.

On Earth, hikers stack stones into cairns to mark the safe way for whoever comes next. REDCAIRN turns the rover's stops into cairns. This is the first trail on Mars a person can follow out, and follow home.

anchorResources.name: Mars Trek
anchorResources.role: The planning map is built on Mars Trek's own tiles (HiRISE 25 cm, CTX, THEMIS night infrared, MOLA + HRSC colour height, the USGS geology service), and every height in the app (the 1 m elevation model of the walk, the crater, the 360° horizon) comes from Mars Trek services.

anchorResources.name: USGS planetary geologic mapping
anchorResources.role: The Rock units layer on the planning map (USGS SIM 3292 via Mars Trek): Mount Sharp (Htu) inside the crater's impact unit (AHi). Htu is the unit under the whole walk.

anchorResources.name: Curiosity's proposed path up Mount Sharp
anchorResources.role: The planning map's 'Curiosity's whole climb' layer and the intro, where the line draws itself over Mount Sharp rendered in 3D: the route the team planned up Mount Sharp, as Curiosity actually drove it, landing to sol 5,073. Our walk follows its 2025–26 stretch.

anchorResources.name: Worldview
anchorResources.role: Each cairn named after a place on Earth (Altadena, Valle de la Luna, Nevado Sajama, the Atacama) links to that place in Worldview, on the map and in the 3D ground view.

anchorResources.name: Perseverance raw images
anchorResources.role: Perseverance's newest raw image, fetched live, and its Navcam photo at every stop of the second walk, Jezero (beta), which the same engine builds from Jezero's own maps.

question.title: Was there life in the lake?
question.text: Jezero held a lake 3.5 billion years ago. Perseverance is sealing rock in tubes so it can be studied on Earth. Your walk goes to the first rock it kept.
question.factCheck: No sign of life has been confirmed. The cores are waiting to be studied.
